approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from scored survivors. It fits a Gaussian process to all real observations using molecular fingerprint counts, generates fresh graph edits, and retains unpurchased fresh graphs for one more decision. At each announcement it compares a Thompson-sampled batch with up to thirty-two substitutions. For each candidate batch, it simulates observations, conditions a second decision on those outcomes, chooses that future batch from retained graphs with sixteen shared samples, and values it using thirty-two independent samples. It buys the current batch with greatest estimated two-batch best-score gain. When the next real decision arrives, it generates more graphs and starts a new rollout. Thus the future policy it priced can be replaced before it is used, even though its graphs remain available.
approach.novelty: Add executed two-stage rollout recourse: save the selected first-batch model state, retained support and random base vectors, then use the actual first observations to choose and buy the previously specified second-step policy once. After that second batch, plan again from all real observations. The distinction is a commitment to the valued decision rule, including its support and scale. It does not extend the horizon or increase the Monte Carlo resolution. There are no same-Parent siblings in the frozen brief. Concurrent work changes learned edit admissions, screens coherent-path purchases, or changes a GIBBON terminal decision; none executes this retained-support recourse. Commitment may improve the connection between modeled value and realized progress, but it can also forgo useful fresh graphs.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-201fe3876d7a values an outcome-dependent retained-only second-batch policy but does not execute that policy after real feedback. Its external/observed_rollout.py::allocate prices greedy_policy on newly born unpurchased retained support using the saved first-step scale and noisy conditional covariance; its optimize.py::Evolution.suggest instead refits with all new real labels and calls allocate again over incoming carry plus fresh graphs. This is a decision-law mismatch established by code, not an inference from overlap with arbitrary fantasy outcomes. The complete Parent retains real-GP fitting, genuine outcome conditioning and physical carry: all 435 allocations succeeded, 378/420 chosen future policies varied across simulated first outcomes, 225/420 current sets differed from passive immediate-only choices, and all 62671 nonterminal carried identities arrived. Nevertheless its complete equal-session adjacent-two-batch progress was 0.02399560213969095 versus 0.027628024236935136 on n-cf8d309c06de; its registered prediction remains refuted. The available-seed endpoint mean is 0.557967625855474, population SD 0.00521907778349108 and paired delta against that code ancestor/formal Anchor is -0.049062690355657024. No incomplete replica or missing carry explains this result. The earlier 5203/67200 fantasy-membership purchases are descriptive and do not estimate policy-failure probability. The fresh-step alternatives sacrificed by commitment may be valuable; alignment is a testable causal mechanism, not evidence of benefit. Read-only rechecks of all Search summaries, run logs, Parent task logs and both nodes trajectories are in policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/plan/parent-evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files, which list each underlying file and preserve its hash. Parent analysis is nodes/n-201fe3876d7a/analysis.json; the frozen source review is policy/scratch/round76-search-policy/evidence-review.json. The independently reduced Parent window mean is 0.023995602139690955 (rounding only); the frozen falsifier uses its registered 0.02399560213969095.

Resolve all exact ties, including zero marginal gains, by the smallest saved retained local index; no new draws, within-B conditioning, evaluation-panel selection or refitted normalization enters this choice. finding_summary.headline: Saved recourse executed exactly, but two-batch progress and final score fell
finding_summary.insights:
Executing the valued continuation removes the Parent’s documented control-law mismatch, but alignment alone did not improve useful search progress in this host. Every committed batch differed from its same-state fresh replan, with only 184 of 2100 purchases shared; the passive plans would select 1517 newly born identities that commitment could not buy. Their unbought outcomes are unknown, so this does not prove the excluded alternatives were better. The limitation is more specific than absent feedback: 879 of 2100 recourse selection positions had exactly zero modeled marginal gain and were filled by the fixed tie rule. The independent saved model predicted mean recourse gain 0.0072415, while the realized mean was 0.0037150 and 167 of 210 second batches made no incumbent improvement. This is evidence of weak useful discrimination in the purchased continuation and selected-stream model optimism, not proof that every posterior estimate is miscalibrated. A ranking or utility model that distinguishes that zero-value tail, or a control scheme that explicitly prices regenerated future support, could address the measured limitation; neither alternative was tested here.

Source-relative positive gain increased from 0.0030020 to 0.0037830 overall and from 0.0011574 to 0.0026413 late, yet the primary progress and endpoint measures declined. Improving on a generating parent therefore did not establish reliable improvement of the best molecule. The chemistry remains an evolving set of favored families rather than universal scaffold collapse. The largest endpoint loss coincides with the first sitagliptin search staying in a modest-scoring indole/geminal-diol neighborhood, while its other searches found stronger compact dicarbonyl and cyclic-appendage families. Across tasks, raw scaffold variety and fewer reactive halogen attachments still coexist with narrow favorable neighborhoods, unresolved stereochemistry and difficult ring geometries. A proposal operator that can move coherently among ring/linker families while preserving useful group placement addresses that structural limitation, but the chemical associations do not identify the controller’s causal contribution.

Both borrowed elements—outcome-conditioned observed-best planning and separation of temporary calculations from real labels—operated. This result rejects the useful-progress prediction for this saved-support commitment under the inherited GP and generator. It leaves broader nonmyopic search, the value of fresh-support-aware planning, and the separate effects of retained components open; it does not end the approach.
finding_summary.results:
All 210 committed second batches executed the registered rule after genuine first-batch feedback. Every saved-support identity arrived, every ordered choice and exact tie matched independent reconstruction, and all 4350 purchases fed the ordinary real archive. Nevertheless, mean realized best-score gain over all 420 adjacent two-batch windows fell from 0.0239956 to 0.0228596; zero-progress windows rose from 135 to 151. The 210 nonoverlapping committed pairs also declined, from 0.0246612 to 0.0236331. This triggers the registered useful-progress falsifier despite successful execution. Seed 0 progress fell substantially, while seeds 1 and 2 increased slightly or moderately; all sessions remain in the result.

Final macro mean fell from 0.5579676 to 0.5405544, a paired delta of -0.0174133 against the separate +0.002 target. Three task/seed endpoints improved and twelve declined; population SD increased from 0.0052191 to 0.0338771. Against the formal Anchor the delta is -0.0664760. The protocol paired task-regression rule triggers no task regression against either comparator, which does not establish score success. All 15 sessions completed the full 300-call budget with no rejection, timeout, fallback or incomplete pair. The separate global criterion requiring the formal Anchor itself as code Parent remains inapplicable to this descendant.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and cyclic-amine families with fewer reactive halogen attachments, but unresolved stereochemistry and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-59436e1eec8f has complete Child evaluation and complete pairing with its actual code Parent n-201fe3876d7a according to the frozen context.comparison. The formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is a different node and is not substituted for this chemical comparator. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent Search trajectories were read; no requested paths, tasks or paired comparisons are missing. Each node contributes 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules across the five objectives and Search seeds 0/1/2, separately from the supplied initial records. These files describe accepted evaluated products, not unpurchased graph pools or rejected proposals. The Child digest has ring-closure rates 0.9713-0.9862 and aromatic-token rates 0.9621-0.9782: these are fractions of SMILES containing the feature, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. The chemistry is rich in substituted indoles, fused nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heterocycles, quinoline-like aromatic blocks, cyclic amines and lactams. Overall median heavy-atom counts range from 25 to 38 across tasks; favored neighborhoods are usually substantially narrower than the full size distribution. RDKit 2023.09.6 structural readings find 463 Child molecules with N-halogen bonds, 124 with O-halogen bonds and 6 with acyl halides, versus 794, 236 and 79 in the Parent. Those reductions do not establish overall chemical tractability: the Child still has 538 N-N-single-bond graphs, 88 peroxide-containing graphs and 9 with a triple bond in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms. The corresponding Parent counts are 658, 54 and zero. There are 57 Child graphs containing a perceived all-aromatic-atom ring of at most four atoms, versus 30 in the Parent; this flag does not assert aromaticity of every bond in that ring. All Child graphs have net formal charge zero and none has an assigned tetrahedral centre, although 2,355 have at least one unassigned centre, versus 1,785 in the Parent. Neutral drawings do not establish solution protonation states. The Child has 90 molecules with at most six heavy atoms and 72 above sixty, versus 127 and 107 in the Parent; neither size tail enters any Child pooled highest-score decile. Broad raw topology variation coexists with repeated favored scaffold families, so moderate structural diversity is more accurate than a universal collapse. Drug-likeness and synthetic plausibility are qualitative readings of complete structures; no synthesis, stability, strain-energy, pKa or biological-activity measurement is inferred. Score gradients and Parent contrasts below are associations in dependent Search trajectories, not component attribution or mechanism-activation conclusions. Pooled deciles contain 87 of 870 optimizer records per task; per-seed deciles contain 29 of 290. Sorting uses score, Search seed, then evaluation; ties can straddle a decile boundary, so these are descriptive fixed-size groups. Sources: policy/requests/r0076-03-improve-L01-molecular-assess-1a4778b6c53b42ef.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/pooled-descriptor-summary.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/build_audits.py. The manifest records the original request-listed staging paths and hashes; the cited Child copies preserve those bytes inside the run. Each task below cites its underlying Child and published Parent files as well as its per-seed audits. SMARTS flags overlap and are structural observations, not measured chemical failure rates.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly substituted indole carboxanilides: a fused aromatic indole joined through an amide to a phenyl or azaaryl ring, with methoxy, methyl, vinyl and amino substituents. Optimizer products span 1-50 heavy atoms, with median 25; the pooled highest-score decile spans 23-26 and usually has three rings and fifteen aromatic atoms. Seed 0 favors a bromophenyl carboxanilide with an additional N-bromo methylamino substituent; seed 1 favors N-chloro carboxamides; seed 2 favors N-bromo carboxamides. The top decile contains 9 typed and 5 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus 12 and 5 in the Parent. The recognizable indole/aryl-amide framework is synthetically more convincing than its frequent N-halogen substitution. Evidence files, paired Search seeds 0, 1, 2: policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-201fe3876d7a/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-201fe3876d7a/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-03-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-201fe3876d7a/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 362 of 870 optimizer molecules and 78 of the top 87, versus Parent counts 328 and 59 under the same decile tie rule. The N-bromo amide in the best molecules is a reactivity concern, not evidence of a stable final medicinal product.

Twenty-one optimizer products have at most six heavy atoms; the poor-score tail also contains oversized duplicated aromatic amides. Useful heteroatom placement is not maintained through all deletion and growth products.
missing_features: Comparable high-score alternatives to the repeatedly used indole/aryl-amide geometry are sparsely represented; only five generic scaffold patterns occur in the highest-score decile. This is limited favorable-family breadth, not absence of aromatic rings.

Chemically ordinary polar substitutions that preserve the favorable arrangement without N-halogen attachment are not consistently represented among leaders. The trajectory does not identify a unique missing target-specific functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Seed 2 evaluations 213 and 298, positional variants bearing vinyl/methyl/methoxy groups and an N-bromo amide, tie at 0.4484138510190879. A similarly compact chlorinated variant at seed 2 evaluation 295 scores 0.20930297426595773, showing that ring count and mere possession of the amide are insufficient. The 48-heavy-atom duplicated indole-anilide at seed 0 evaluation 46 scores 1.160424008177892e-23, and NBr at seed 0 evaluation 222 scores zero. The visible gradient favors a compact, specifically substituted aromatic/amide arrangement rather than scaffold duplication or deletion to tiny fragments. The Parent additionally favored indene carboxamides in one seed; its favorable chemistry was also heavily affected by N-halogen substitution. Child best observed scores by Search seed 0, 1, 2 are 0.40497388700123543, 0.4163503402962837, 0.4484138510190879; published code-Parent values are 0.41885833432199493, 0.4387992465191, 0.4519753205796759.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds occupy distinct chemical families. Seed 1 leaders are compact fused N/O carbonyl heterobicycles with linked azaaryl rings, formate esters and fluorine; the best has 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including a four-membered ring containing a triple bond. Seed 0 instead grows repeated N-methyl carbonyl heterocycles and azaaromatic blocks joined through unsaturated or methylene links; its best has 84 heavy atoms. Seed 2 produces densely fused N-rich diones with aryl ethers, small oxygen-containing ring fusions and thiocarbonyl decoration; its best has 47 heavy atoms and eleven perceived rings. The full output spans 1-115 heavy atoms, median 38; the top decile spans 31-45, median 34, and contains 26 typed/13 generic scaffolds versus Parent 22/17. These are heteroatom-rich aromatic assemblies, but several complete topologies are difficult synthetic propositions. liabilities: Nine optimizer graphs have a triple bond in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, and eight occur in the top 87; the Parent has none. The best molecule contains a four-membered alkyne ring, a serious geometry and persistence concern despite its accepted SMILES.

Forty-eight products exceed sixty heavy atoms, versus one hundred in the Parent; none is in the Child top decile. Repeated fused heterocycles, long unsaturated linkers and difficult small oxygen-containing rings remain present.

Formate esters, nitroso substituents and peroxide linkages occur in the wider output; their formal graph validity does not establish stability or synthetic accessibility. Twenty-four products contain at most six heavy atoms.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial carbonyl heterocycle/aryl ester scores 0.548381482770623. Formaldehyde at seed 1 evaluation 210 sits at 0.5, while the compact azaaryl/formate leader at seed 1 evaluation 291 scores 0.619656558275484. The 115-heavy-atom product at seed 0 evaluation 236 scores 0.5829969613134383; repeated heterocycle growth does not reproduce the compact family. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
